description: Hand-computed Jensen-Shannon divergence (log base 2, so JSD is in [0, 1]) and model_agreement_score cases for SPEC_v2 section 7. JSD(P, Q) = 0.5 * KL(P || M) + 0.5 * KL(Q || M), M = 0.5 * (P + Q), with 0 * log(0) = 0. A channel missing from a distribution has credit 0. Each value was worked by hand (see its derivation) before the implementation existed; tests compare with an absolute tolerance of 1e-12.

jsd_cases.name: identical
jsd_cases.derivation: P = Q, so M = P and every term is p * log2(p / p) = 0. JSD = 0.

jsd_cases.name: fully_disjoint_single_channel
jsd_cases.derivation: M = {email: 0.5, social: 0.5}. KL(P||M) = 1 * log2(1 / 0.5) = 1; KL(Q||M) = 1 by symmetry. JSD = 0.5 * 1 + 0.5 * 1 = 1.

jsd_cases.name: fully_disjoint_multi_channel
jsd_cases.derivation: Supports do not overlap, so M = P/2 on P's channels and Q/2 on Q's. KL(P||M) = sum p * log2(p / (p/2)) = sum p * 1 = 1; likewise KL(Q||M) = 1. JSD = 1. Any two disjoint distributions reach the base-2 maximum of 1.

jsd_cases.name: explicit_zero_equals_missing_channel
jsd_cases.derivation: Same distributions as partial_overlap_one_shared_channel: an explicit 0 credit and an absent channel are the same point on the simplex, and 0 * log2(0 / m) = 0. JSD = 0.5.

jsd_cases.name: unnormalized_weights_are_normalized_first
jsd_cases.derivation: Dividing each by its total gives P = {email: 0.5, social: 0.5} and Q = {social: 0.5, organic: 0.5}, the partial_overlap_one_shared_channel case. JSD = 0.5.

agreement_cases.name: three_models_two_agree
agreement_cases.derivation: 3 * 2 / 2 = 3 pairs: (1,2) identical = 0, (1,3) disjoint = 1, (2,3) disjoint = 1. Mean = 2/3. Agreement = 1 - 2/3 = 1/3.

test_data_csv_five_models.derivation: Recorded regression value, not hand-computed: the time_decay credits are irrational. Computed from the default-parameter credits of all five models on test_data.csv (credits unchanged from v1 and docs/b0-baseline.md) over 10 pairs, and cross-checked independently as 1 - mean(scipy.spatial.distance.jensenshannon(p, q, base=2) ** 2) = 0.883199552108466 (difference 1.1e-16; scipy returns the distance, so it is squared).
